title: Electric Field — Interactive Concept Map
topicTitle: Electric Field — Mindmap and Conceptual Hierarchy
notes: Comprehensive conceptual breakdown of electric field, field lines, electric dipoles, electric flux, and Gauss's law applications.
Covers core NEB formulas: E = F/q₀, E = kq/r², dipole fields (axial E = 2kp/r³ vs equatorial E = kp/r³), flux Φ = ∮ E · dA, and Gauss's law Φ = Q_enc / ε₀.
Derives key geometric fields: infinite line charge (E = λ / (2πε₀r)), infinite plane sheet (E = σ / (2ε₀)), and spherical shell (E_inside = 0, E_outside = kQ/r²).

subtopics.name: Field Vector & Point Charges
points: Definition: E = lim(q₀→0) F/q₀ (SI unit: N/C or V/m)
Field of isolated point charge: E = (1/4πε₀) · (q/r²) r̂
Superposition principle: E_net = ∑ E_i for discrete charges
Continuous distributions: E = (1/4πε₀) ∫ dq/r² r̂ (line, surface, volume)

subtopics.name: Electric Field Lines
points: Continuous imaginary curves tangent to local field vector E
Originate at positive charges, terminate on negative charges
Lines never intersect (uniqueness of force direction)
Areal density represents field magnitude
Never form closed loops (electrostatic field is conservative: ∮ E · dr = 0)

subtopics.name: Dipole Moment & External Field
points: Dipole moment vector: p = q(2a), directed from -q to +q
Torque in uniform external field: τ = p × E (aligns dipole with field)
Potential energy: U = -p · E (minimum at θ = 0°, maximum at θ = 180°)
Non-uniform field: experiences net force F = (p · ∇)E and torque

subtopics.name: Dipole Electric Field
points: Axial position (end-on): E_axial = (1/4πε₀) · (2p/r³) along p (r ≫ a)
Equatorial position (broadside): E_equatorial = -(1/4πε₀) · (p/r³) opposite p
Ratio relation: E_axial = 2 · E_equatorial at equal distance r
Distance dependency: E ∝ 1/r³ (falls off faster than point charge 1/r²)

subtopics.name: Electric Flux
points: Elemental flux: dΦ = E · dA = E dA cos(θ)
Total flux: Φ = ∬ E · dA (SI unit: N·m²/C or V·m)
Outward normal convention: positive for exiting flux, negative for entering

subtopics.name: Gauss's Theorem
points: Integral statement: ∮_S E · dA = Q_enclosed / ε₀
Differential form (Maxwell 1): ∇ · E = ρ / ε₀
Independent of Gaussian surface size and shape
External charges produce zero net flux across closed surface
Directly equivalent to inverse-square Coulomb's law

subtopics.name: Infinite Line Charge
points: Cylindrical Gaussian surface of radius r, length L
End caps contribute zero flux (E ⊥ dA)
Curved surface: E · (2πrL) = λL / ε₀
Field formula: E = λ / (2πε₀r) (inversely proportional to r)

subtopics.name: Infinite Plane Sheet
points: Cylindrical pillbox of cross-section A piercing plane
Curved surface flux = 0; two end caps: 2EA = σA / ε₀
Field formula: E = σ / (2ε₀) (independent of distance r)
Between oppositely charged plates: E = σ / ε₀; outside: E = 0

subtopics.name: Charged Spherical Shell & Solid Sphere
points: Thin shell outside (r ≥ R): E = (1/4πε₀) · (Q/r²)
Thin shell inside (r < R): E = 0 (electrostatic shielding / Faraday cage)
Uniform non-conducting solid sphere inside (r ≤ R): E = (ρr) / (3ε₀) ∝ r
